cadOnly: HEAD v the build before the drawing feature (36f6f7d3): 8 parts identical to the last decimal; real-parts baseline (40 parts): no drift
overall: The offline drawing reader is safe to put in front of engineers: no drawing leaves the machine, nothing it reads reaches a cost until an engineer confirms it, and CAD-only costing is unchanged. It is not yet an accurate reader. On 44 genuine public drawings it reads 30 % of what they state (58 % on CAD-exported PDFs with selectable text, 22 % on text drawn as curves, 5 % on scans); 69 % of what it reads is right (85 % on selectable-text PDFs). Material is now read on 32 of 37 drawings. Cost accuracy is NOT validated: no real price exists for any tested part.
keyFindings: Data protection — PASS after fix. The audit found one Critical defect: in AI-led or Compare mode a PDF drawing was sent to the AI model while the screen said nothing leaves the server. Fixed: no drawing is sent to a model in any mode, and a model's reading of a drawing is discarded. Proven by tests with every outbound socket blocked.

Unconfirmed values never reach a cost — PASS. Across every costing run, an unreviewed drawing costs exactly what no drawing costs (£11.033029 v £11.033029); confirmed drawing answers cost exactly what the same answers typed by hand cost.

CAD-only regression — PASS. 8 real parts on 8 commodities are bit-identical to the build before the drawing feature; the 40-part real-parts baseline shows no drift; the full suite passes (5,913 tests passed (362 files)).

Extraction is selective, not complete. Strict precision / recall after the fixes: 69.1 % / 30.1 % overall (83.3 % / 26.6 % before). Reliable: material (100 % precision, 86.5 % recall), general tolerance, coating, notes, fits (6 of 7 right). Unreliable: title block (17 % recall), GD&T (4.7 % recall — symbols drawn as geometry are not read), dimensions on curves and scans, roughness.

The precision fall is one drawing family: NX stroke-font sheets now go through OCR (they read nothing before) and give 139 wrong dimension readings against 35 right. Every one is marked 'needs checking' and none can reach a cost, but the engineer has to reject them.

Reconciliation: 12 pass / 6 partial / 2 fail of 20 tests (6 / 8 / 5 before). Conflicts are raised and never settled for the engineer; corrections persist and are traced (who, when, why); a review sent with another drawing is skipped. Not detected: a drawing paired with the wrong CAD when no holes are read, and a revision mismatch (revisions are never compared).

Costing effect (indicative): where the drawing's material was confirmed, the cost moved by +17 % to +58 % on 7 of 13 rows — largely because the CAD-only run had assumed the wrong material (plastic from a 'PP-' part number in the file name, a defect now fixed). This shows the drawing replacing an assumption, not that either figure is accurate.

Exports — PASS after fixes. Screen = core PDF = audit pack = Excel to the penny on every costing checked (£15.20, £17.80, £24.92); drawing table matches the review panel row for row and now prints who decided, when and why. Fixed on the way: two different confidence grades for one costing, stale 'no drawing is read' text, a clipped stamp, a dropped depth symbol.

52 defects were found by three independent runs; 32 fixed with a test that failed first, 5 partly fixed, 15 open (none Critical or High; 8 Medium, 12 Low). The most consequential open items: machining costs the material FAMILY only (304 stainless is costed as EN8 carbon steel); blank development blocks the server for about 40 s (every user waits); revision and wrong-CAD pairing are not checked.
method: Independence: the code audit was done by a reviewer who had not built the feature, against the original brief; the 44 truth files were written from rendered drawing images by two reviewers who never ran the reader and never saw its code; measurement and reliability runs are scripts that can be re-run.

Test material: 26 genuine public CAD + drawing pairs and 3 drawing-only sets, every one with its licence and the evidence that drawing and model are the same part (register in the workbook). Sources: NIST MBE PMI test cases and D2MI parts (public domain), LulzBot TAZ 6 (CC BY-SA 4.0), OpenEAI robot arm (BSD-3), SeedMint jig (GPL-3.0), the DOE/NASA Automotive Stirling Engine drawings (public use). The project's own generated drawings were NOT counted as evidence.

Not accessible: GrabCAD, TraceParts, PARTcommunity and 3D ContentCentral need an account; NHTSA blocks automated access; Bosch Motorsport and catalogue vendors' terms forbid it. No login wall, bot check or licence was worked around. Consequence: the only automotive drawings are the Stirling-engine scans.

Three workflows on identical inputs: A — CAD only (blocking questions answered with the tool's own leaning, recorded); B — drawing only (the reader, scored against truth); C — CAD + drawing reviewed as a careful engineer would from the truth file (confirm right readings, correct wrong ones, reject fabricated ones). UK, 10,000 a year, 5 years, DAP, the built-in rate book, 10 Nov 2026, AI switched off throughout.

Scoring: precision = correct ÷ (correct + wrong); recall = correct ÷ items stated on the drawing; a reading in a group the truth marks complete that is not on the drawing counts as wrong (fabricated); a missing value is never counted correct. Lenient scoring differs from strict only where the truth writer and the reader file the same diameter under two names (2 readings); no value is relaxed.

Fix and re-test in three rounds; every fix has a test that failed before it, and after each round the full suite, the real-parts baseline and a live browser run with AI off were repeated. The reader fixes were developed on half the drawing families and checked on the other half (held-out material recall 79 %, 15 of 19).

extractionReading: What improved: material (0 → 32 of 37), coating (53 → 84 % recall), quality marks (39 → 65 %). What did not: title block (17 % recall — most of these sheets have no conventional title block, and curve-text cells are not read), GD&T (5 % — symbols drawn as geometry), threads (39 %), dimensions (38 % recall, 57 % precision after stroke-font OCR). A reading's status is the safeguard: every OCR reading needs checking and nothing reaches a cost unconfirmed.
costingReading: Every change from A to C is explained by an answer the drawing supplied (material family or grade, finish). No wrong reading reached a cost in any run. Machining asks the material family only, so a stated grade (304, 6061-T6) is costed as the family's representative grade and listed as not costed — a cost-model limitation the drawing exposes. The 'PP-' file-name defect made the CAD-only figure for two LulzBot parts plastic; it is fixed in 90022108 (proven by a unit test on the real file names), so those two A figures will move; they were not re-costed live after the fix.
accuracy: Independent costing accuracy cannot be assessed: there is no purchase price, supplier quote or cycle-time sheet for any tested part, and none was invented. Every £ in this report is INDICATIVE.

What the comparison does show: on 7 of 13 cost rows the drawing replaced an assumed material (and on two a finish) with a stated one; on 3 it changed nothing; 3 were refused by the tool's own route check in both A and C; it never made a cost depend on an unconfirmed reading.
What it does not show: that the CAD + drawing figure is closer to what a part costs. A difference between A and C is a difference in inputs, not evidence of accuracy.

To measure accuracy: enter real prices for real parts in calculator/scripts/actuals/cad-actuals-input.csv (price, volume, life, country, finish, source) and run npx tsx scripts/cad-actuals.ts then npm run accuracy. Ten to twenty parts per commodity, with their drawings, would give a first error band per commodity.

Against: the reader finds 30 % of what a drawing states (58 % on CAD-exported PDFs); GD&T, title blocks and dimensions on curve-text or scanned sheets are weak; no automotive CAD + drawing pair could be tested; cost accuracy is unvalidated; four Medium defects remain open that matter in daily use (machining costs the family only, the server blocks for ~40 s during blank development, revision and wrong-CAD pairing unchecked).

Enter purchase prices for 10–20 parts that also have drawings (scripts/actuals/cad-actuals-input.csv) and report the error band, labelled per commodity.
Demonstrate on CAD-exported PDFs with selectable text (the class that reads 85 % right), and say plainly that scans and curve-text sheets are read poorly and always need checking.
Fix or disclose the open Medium items: grade on the machining route (304 costed as EN8), blank development blocking the server (multi-user deployment), revision and wrong-model checks.
Do not present the CAD + drawing cost change as an accuracy gain: it is an input change until real prices are compared.

answers.q: 1. Does the reader genuinely interpret engineering information, or mainly OCR and text extraction?
answers.a: Both, with a clear line. It extracts text (exact PDF text, or OCR) and then interprets it with standards tables: ISO 286 fits into limits, ISO 8062-3 casting grades and EN 10243 forging grades into the tolerance class, material designations into a family and rate-book grade (EN / AA / EN 1706 / GB / JIS numbering), coating names and thicknesses into the finish routes, hole and thread callouts matched to the 3D model's holes, inch values converted. It does not interpret GD&T symbols drawn as geometry, weld symbols, roughness symbols or views and sections, and it does not decide the process.

answers.q: 2. Which parameters are reliable, which are not?
answers.a: Reliable (high precision; recall as stated): material 100 % / 86.5 %, general tolerance 100 % / 59 %, coating 100 % / 84 %, notes 99 % / 44 %, fits 86 % / 86 % (6 of 7). Unreliable: title block (100 % right but 17 % found), GD&T (4.7 % found), threads (69 % / 39 %), dimensions (57 % / 38 %, much worse on curves and scans), roughness (0 of 12).

answers.q: 3. Does combining 2D drawings with 3D CAD improve engineering-data completeness?
answers.a: Yes, for what the 3D model cannot carry: on the costed pairs the drawing supplied material, temper, finish and coating, which the CAD-only run had to assume (and in two cases assumed wrongly). Measured: 7 of 13 cost rows had an assumed input replaced by a stated one. It adds nothing on drawings whose text it cannot read.

answers.q: 4. Does it demonstrably improve should-costing accuracy against independent reference data?
answers.a: Not demonstrated. There is no independent reference cost for any tested part, so accuracy is unmeasured. The tool's costs changed by +17 % to +58 % where the material was supplied — evidence that the drawing matters, not that the result is more accurate.

answers.q: 5. Which commodities and component types have actually been validated?
answers.a: Drawing extraction: machined aluminium and steel plates and blocks, bent and flat sheet-metal parts, a cast-like housing, a non-rigid ring and scanned engine parts — 44 drawings. Costing A v C: machining and sheet metal only. Not validated with drawings: castings with a stated material, forgings, mouldings, rubber, welded assemblies, brakes, steering, suspension, wheels, electrical, battery, EDU, transmission.

answers.q: 6. Has existing CAD-only functionality remained unaffected?
answers.a: Yes. Bit-identical costs on 8 real parts against the build before the feature, no drift on the 40-part baseline, the full suite passing. The only CAD-only change is deliberate: a 'PP-' / 'PC-' part number in a file name is no longer read as polypropylene / polycarbonate.

answers.q: 7. Are the PDF and Excel outputs technically reliable?
answers.a: Yes after the fixes: screen, core PDF, audit pack and workbook agree to the penny on every costing checked; the drawing table matches the review panel; engineering symbols print (Ø, ±, °, µm; GD&T and depth symbols as words in the PDF, Unicode in Excel); who / when / why are printed. Four export defects were found and fixed with tests.

answers.q: 8. What must be fixed before presenting to the Cost Engineering Director?
answers.a: Measure extraction on real JLR drawings inside JLR; enter real prices for a sample of parts; fix or disclose the open Medium defects (machining grade, blank development blocking the server, revision / wrong-model checks, stroke-font OCR noise); demonstrate on selectable-text PDFs and state the limits.

answers.q: 9. Ready for an internal trial, a Director demonstration or production?
answers.a: Suitable for controlled internal testing. It is safe and traceable enough for engineers to try on real JLR drawings inside JLR, which is also the step that produces the evidence a Director demonstration needs. Not yet production: accuracy is unmeasured on real drawings and real prices, and four Medium defects remain.
